correctness.rationale: For KG(n,2), n>=5, vertex-to-edge distance is 0 for either edge endpoint doubleton, 2 for the other four doubletons lying in its four-point support, and 1 outside. Thus for two graph edges with supports meeting in h points, the resolving neighborhood has size 12-2*C(h,2)+q, where q is the number of intersection doubletons in exactly one endpoint matching. Independent examination of the finite matching choices on prescribed union supports t=4,5,6,7,8 gives respectively (size,count): (4,3),(6,30),(8,60),(10,225),(11,180),(12,630),(12,315); unique union support yields the six-term claimed polynomial. Uniform weights 1/4 are feasible and three distinct-matching-pair inequalities on each 4-support yield the matching LP dual lower bound C(n,2)/4. Directly independently written BFS reproduces complete histograms n=5,6,7, not a proof for all n. Empty binomial terms make all formulas valid at n=5.
residual_risks: Independent computations are bounded and not proofs of all-parameter conclusions.
Structural published hypotheses cited in the package remain part of the proof premises.

value.rationale: Exact six-term pairwise resolving-neighborhood polynomial is a natural complete ambiguity invariant for an infinite canonical edge-location graph family; beyond the previously known scalar the seven overlap types expose how four-point supports lose distance information. Tight matching LP witness makes the exact fractional optimum reproducible and intrinsic, not an arbitrary computational slice.
residual_risks: Future priority discovery may revise originality; this does not make the motivated natural invariant intrinsically uninteresting.

limitations: Two-element Kneser graphs and fractional edge resolving, n>=5; no higher-rank Kneser, integral dimension, optimizer uniqueness or universal literature certification.
